lesson_title: Hand Off Before You Feel It: The Spinal Cord's Secret Shortcut
hook_text: You let go of the hot pot before you felt the burn. Your brain was not even consulted.
clip_script: Your nervous system is the marshal at the taxi rank. Brain and spinal cord in the middle, the central nervous system. Nerves running to every corner, the peripheral system, carrying electrical pulses at up to 120 metres a second. Sensory neurons bring news in from your eyes, ears and skin. Motor neurons carry orders out to the muscles. Now grab a burning pot handle. Receptors in your fingertip fire. A sensory neuron races to the spinal cord. And here is the trick: the cord does not wait for the brain. It passes the message straight to a motor neuron, the arm muscle contracts, hand off. Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, effector. A reflex arc, in a few hundredths of a second. The brain hears about it afterwards, which is why the pain arrives late. Everything else goes the long way through the brain: cerebrum thinks, cerebellum balances, medulla breathes. Neurons do not grow back. Wear the helmet. Click the seat belt. And drop a ruler into a friend's hand after one drink and watch how far it falls.
visual_style: A rank marshal with a glowing brain and spine; a hand reaches for a pot, a pulse zips up the arm to the spinal cord and straight back down while a slower pulse crawls toward the brain; a ruler drops through an open hand.
pacing: Quick setup, a slowed-down beat on the reflex arc, a rapid brain tour, a snap ending on the ruler.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the five-part pathway for any reflex.
